# What you can do with only drawings, only process knowledge, or both

**Demonstration reference.** This compares the repository's TE and OPEN100 tracks, not outputs promised for
arbitrary company inputs. Use [supported workflows](WORKFLOWS.md) for reusable routes and [project status](STATUS.md)
for unfinished implementation and validation.

*Generated by `scripts/deliverables_matrix.py` from [deliverables_matrix.json](deliverables_matrix.json); edit the
JSON, then run `python scripts/deliverables_matrix.py --write`.*

The two main tracks have opposite halves of the picture. **TE** has process knowledge (a model checked against the
simulator source, and recorded simulator replay) and no original drawing. **OPEN100** has 12 real drawings and
no process data. Most of a digital twin starter kit needs only the structure, and drawings carry structure: equipment,
connections, flow arrows, off-page links, isolation valves. Values, normal bands, alarms and replay need process data,
so OPEN100 can't have them, and the table says so instead of faking them. What OPEN100 gets from its drawings alone is
in [OPEN100_STRUCTURAL.md](OPEN100_STRUCTURAL.md): flow direction read from arrowheads, flags and pump ports
(361 of 1,133 process links; the rest stay undirected), the 12 sheets stitched into one plant, an ISA-101-style mimic,
a 3D orientation tour and a LOTO isolation view on the real drawing (a mockup, not a procedure: a valve the
extraction missed is not on the list).

| Asset model (equipment, instruments, connections, hierarchy) | **Done**: transcribed from the published process; every tag checked against the simulator source (36 confirmed, 1 corrected) and every unit, stream, direction and tag owner against its balances and flow lines (51 confirmed, 4 corrected, 1 unresolvable of 56); 0 items reviewed by operations ([te_topology_check.md](../out/te_topology_check.md), [te_source_check.md](../out/te_source_check.md)) | **Done**: extracted from the drawings: 2,886 items, all unverified until reviewed, risk tiers 1,811 green / 698 amber / 377 red (22 instruments held at amber by the safety floor); on six held-out drawings (which also chose the method) symbols found F1 0.93, connections 0.87, review load 20.1 per 100, all means of five round-5 runs (the earlier single round-2 run scored 17.8) ([review_queue.csv](../out/twin/r2-tiles-trace/codex/review_queue.csv), [replicates_r5_holdout-a.md](../out/replicates_r5_holdout-a.md)) |
| Tag text read from drawings | **Done**: a round trip on the generated sheets: every tag read on clean sheets by both models, 14% (GPT) and 49% (Claude) at the worst scan level; an upper bound for clean house-style drawings, not real-plant accuracy ([roundtrip_scores.md](../out/te_pid/roundtrip_scores.md)) | **Not possible**: the public answer keys carry no text, so tag reading cannot be scored here; on three DEXPI example sheets with labelled symbols (round 5) GPT read 29 of 33 tags exactly and Claude 28, and on two more both found 99-100% of 145 identifiers from the published tag lists |
| Ignition tags and PI AF asset structure | **Done**: loaded into a lab gateway; the PI Builder sheet (schema v2) is checked offline against the vendor-published conventions, not imported into a PI System ([te_tags.json](../out/ignition/te_tags.json), [pi](../out/pi)) | **Done**: same; instrument tags are placeholders until an I/O list maps them, and placeholder PI rows are left unselected ([tags.json](../out/twin/r2-tiles-trace/codex/ignition/tags.json), [pi](../out/twin/r2-tiles-trace/codex/pi)) |
